title: Bucktown cabarets
summary: He describes Bucktown cabarets with little dance-band music, and Pattengill's 25-cent club.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah. And it still has seafood places.
Yeah. I know that place. It was Frank Brunens.
Well, what did they have at Bucktown the way the music did they?

Well they didn't have any, any uh, uh, spectacular music. Those days Dick, the cabarets weren't like they ought to do. Man you go to a cabaret at Bucktown it costs you thirty, forty dollars to get out of it. And uh, they didn't go in much for dance bands like they do now. There was more drinking boats than anything else. You didn't go in there and drink. That's why I'm telling you Frank Pattengill opened one of the first twenty-five cent clubs that there was. That was around the twenties. When he opened the twenty-five cent club. I don't guess you remember that. No. You remember the honeysuckle then?
